question: Can three executions of one trained native Qwen transformer layer infer an unseen individual's color from three facts with no explicit memory retrieval at inference, beating untouched Qwen Base?
protocol: One unique document per story from publisher bAbI 1.2 English 10k induction. Randomly permute the nine static premises independently before tokenizing every training and evaluation story. Freeze all 128 held-out stories before native work. After Qwen layers 0..14 pool each sentence into four regions and compress it to one latent token. Append the question token. Apply Qwen decoder layer 15 three times with tied native Q/K/V/O LoRA and native causal self-attention and MLP. A lexical logit residual reads the final question token only. There is no hand-coded transition, externally retrieved evidence or per-option pointer in the forward pass. Three support head losses are training-only. Always evaluate the unrestricted full-vocabulary thinking turn and identical answer probes, all ordered prompt IDs, and actual times including sentence encoding. The ordinary complete-prompt Base decoder participates in every trained-arm answer.
gate: At least 8 net generated answers, exact two-sided paired p<.05, at least 4 net common-prefix color probes, and at most 1.50x Base generation seconds. Stop on memory warning or time limit. Only a pass licenses an identically supervised one-layer-execution comparison and subsequent independent replication.
